label: thm:substrate-self-duality
title: Self-duality of the algebraic substrate
html:
Let the substrate algebra A be finite and projective over R and symmetric: its Frobenius form \lambda \colon A \to \mathbf{1} satisfies \lambda(ab) = \lambda(ba). Then \lambda induces a quasi-isomorphism between A and its rigid dualizing complex \omega_A^\bullet:

A \xrightarrow{ \sim } \omega_A^\bullet \quad\text{in } D(A).

The non-degenerate Frobenius pairing \langle a, b \rangle_F = \lambda(\mu(a \otimes b)) defines an A-bimodule map \varphi \colon A \to \omega_A^\bullet whose cone is acyclic. Symmetry is what makes \varphi a map of bimodules. For a Frobenius form that is not symmetric, \lambda(ab) = \lambda(b\,\nu(a)) for the Nakayama automorphism \nu, and the same construction identifies \omega_A^\bullet with the twisted bimodule {}_1A_\nu instead of A [lorenz2011].

This quasi-isomorphism implies a Serre-type duality \mathrm{Ext}^i_A(M, A) \cong H^{d-i}(M)^\vee for finitely generated A-modules M. The composition \varepsilon \circ \mu factors through the Frobenius form, providing a categorical trace on \mathrm{End}(A). Because \omega_A^\bullet is rigid, the quasi-isomorphism is unique.
